transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood PM), Samir Das (AuroraCloud PM), Lena Kowalski (AuroraCloud DevOps), Marco Ruiz (AuroraCloud SE), Ivy Zhang (AuroraCloud Security)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. quick agenda: marketplace listing reqs, reference arch, packaging and test plan.
[00:18] Samir Das: thanks Alex, yep we just want to make sure the listing meets AuroraCloud marketplace requirements and that the reference arch fits our customers who want VPC peering and bring-your-own-key.
[00:30] Priya Patel: perfect, i can walk thru the typical redwood deliverables - we usually provide a hero diagram, architecture doc, deployment templates (helm + terraform), and a reference workload for perf tests.
[00:45] Lena Kowalski: quick question, does Redwood publish an official container image or do partners build their own wrapper? we've seen both patterns on other marketplaces.
[00:55] Alex Chen: good Q. we offer both. for quick listings we can provide an official Redwood runtime image plus an example wrapper. for co-managed joint solutions partners usually keep their image and we provide the integration hooks, e.g., authenticate to redwood via KMS-backed API keys or sso.
[01:12] Marco Ruiz: when you say KMS-backed API keys, do you mean a customer-managed KMS? we need to know for our security review.
[01:20] Priya Patel: yes, we support customer-managed KMS integrations (HSM via partner KMS), and we also have a hosted key option. for private deployments we can integrate with your KMS over a secure channel; there are some networking requirements (outbound to control plane or private control plane option).
[01:40] Ivy Zhang: are those logs and audit records available to us? we need SIEM ingest and long term retention for some compliance customers.
[01:48] Alex Chen: absolutely, audit logs can be exported to your log sink; we support S3, GCS, and partner syslog endpoints. retention is configurable, enterprise add-on.
[02:05] Samir Das: ok noted. next, listing assets. Aurora's marketplace requires a hero image, product copy, pricing tiers, and a verified perf benchmark. how do we want to handle the perf sheet?
[02:20] Diego Morales: we can provide a perf profile for the model variants we recommend, but the partner needs to run a short benchmark in their environment. we usually supply a spreadsheet with token-level cost and latency numbers for a few common seq lengths.
[02:38] Lena Kowalski: would you be able to share that spreadsheet today? even a template will help.
[02:44] Priya Patel: i'll attach the template after the call. it's basically latency p50/p95 by seq length, tokens/sec for batch sizes, and recommended quantization.
[02:58] Marco Ruiz: about deployment packaging, our infra is Kubernetes-based with a Terraform bootstrap for VPC and IAM. can you support a Helm chart and a terraform module that sets up service accounts and network policies?
[03:14] Priya Patel: yes, we have an internal helm chart we use for private deployments; we can sanitize and share a partner-friendly version. for terraform modules we have examples that create service accounts, IAM bindings, and a sample VPC peering config.
[03:30] Alex Chen: small note - the terraform module includes optional autoscaling policy hints. those are tunable by the partner's workload.
[03:38] Samir Das: good. about billing integration - AuroraCloud prefers marketplace metering where usage flows through Aurora's billing. Redwood supports both direct billing and marketplace metering right?
[03:50] Priya Patel: correct. we can integrate with marketplace metering APIs; there is a contract and billing mapping step though. we should align on SKU mapping and pricing tiers.
[04:05] Samir Das: i'll loop in our marketplace ops.
[04:10] [silence / notes]
[04:20] Marco Ruiz: let's dig into networking and fallbacks — if customers are in restricted VPCs, can Redwood run a private control plane or do you require an outbound connection?
[04:30] Priya Patel: two options: private control plane (we give a customer-managed control plane in their VPC) or outbound to our hosted control plane via explicit allowlists. private control plane needs a different license but eliminates outbound egress constraints.
[04:45] Lena Kowalski: are there size/cost implications for private control plane? our finance team will ask.
[04:52] Diego Morales: yes, private control plane involves reserved capacity and a platform fee; we can map it to Dedicated pricing. we'll share a pricing blob.
[05:05] Samir Das: ok that helps. security - Ivy, anything else from your side?
[05:12] Ivy Zhang: i need to confirm SAML SSO support, RBAC mapping, and how keys are rotated. also please share SOC2 scope.
[05:22] Priya Patel: SAML and OIDC are supported; RBAC maps to roles we define in the console and via API. key rotation for customer-managed keys follows your KMS policy, we rotate API tokens and rekey procedures are documented. i'll include the SOC2 summary in the docs.
[05:40] Marco Ruiz: great. on the reference arch, could we walk through a proposed flow?
[05:46] Priya Patel: sure - i have a quick sketch.
[05:50] [05:50] Priya Patel: client app -> AuroraCloud ingress -> customer VPC -> k8s cluster (aurora) -> sidecar/adapter wraps calls and forwards to Redwood endpoint with bearer token -> optional prefix cache in aurora (kv cache) -> request hits Redwood runtime (dedicated or hosted) -> response returns to app. there is also an alternate flow for private control plane where the runtime lives in the customer subnet.
[06:20] Lena Kowalski: that prefix cache — is that something Aurora needs to run or is it provided by Redwood?
[06:26] Priya Patel: prefix/KV cache can be either. we provide a lightweight caching adapter that partners can run to reduce token costs and latency. it's open-sourced as part of the integration pack.
[06:40] Marco Ruiz: does the adapter require sticky session / affinity?
[06:44] Priya Patel: no, it's consistent hashing + local kv; for scale we recommend a replicated cache with affinity but it's not strictly required.
[06:52] [06:52] Marco Ruiz: ok.
[07:00] Samir Das: inventory of deliverables — let's call them: listing assets, helm chart, terraform module, reference arch doc, perf benchmark template, security pack. does that sound right?
[07:14] Alex Chen: yep that's the usual set. additionally we should have a 'Getting Started' guide for an Aurora customer to launch a sample workload.
[07:23] Diego Morales: and a short runbook for fallback — e.g., if dedicated capacity isn't available we automatically route to hosted model variant. mention that in the arch.
[07:35] Ivy Zhang: on the SOC2 and logs front, can we set up a short compliance call after you share the SOC2 summary?
[07:42] Alex Chen: yes, we can schedule a follow-up with our security team.
[07:46] Samir Das: on testing, we want an end-to-end staging run. can Redwood provide a small test harness that fires sample prompts and measures end-to-end latency and costs?
[07:57] Priya Patel: yes. we'll provide a harness (python script + k6 job) that posts requests and measures p50/p95 and token counts.
[08:08] Lena Kowalski: perfect, that will help with certifying the listing.
[08:12] [08:12] Marco Ruiz: any constraints on model versions for marketplace listing? we have customers who want to lock a model to a known quantized variant.
[08:22] Priya Patel: you can pin model versions in the listing; we recommend listing a default model and documenting compatible quantized flavors. also call out supported sequence lengths and recommended batch sizes.
[08:35] Samir Das: good. logistic Q: who's the single point of contact for final assets?
[08:40] Alex Chen: Alex is the AE and will compile assets; Priya handles technical packaging; Diego is product / pricing contact. we've added action items.
[08:50] [brief cross talk — background noise]
[09:05] Samir Das: timeline check: if assets are ready by 3/18 and we do staging 3/23, we can aim for listing submission to Aurora marketplace early April. any blockers?
[09:17] Diego Morales: main blocker would be compliance review; Ivy's team will need to sign off on SOC2 mapping and KMS integration. also marketplace ops sometimes needs a verified perf run in their environment.
[09:30] Ivy Zhang: noted. we'll aim to review as fast as possible but may need a week for internal ops.
[09:38] Marco Ruiz: last technical - network ports and IP ranges for allowlist, do you have a published list?
[09:44] Priya Patel: yes, we maintain an allowlist doc; for private control plane deployments it's minimal. i'll share the CIDR ranges and port list.
[09:55] Alex Chen: ok let's recap. action items: Redwood sends marketplace checklist, helm chart sanitized, terraform module, perf template, reference arch draft. Aurora shares helm chart currently in use, terraform bootstrap snippets, and confirms co-sell vs marketplace billing. schedule staging run.
[10:20] Samir Das: thanks everyone. how about we schedule the compliance deep dive the week after your reference arch draft is out?
[10:28] Ivy Zhang: that works.
[10:30] Alex Chen: great. i'll send calendar invites and post the assets in the shared drive. thanks all.
[10:38] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mishearing (e.g., 'prefix cache' sometimes transcribed as 'prefetch cache'), some proper nouns may be slightly off.
